topics.why: Create a CloudWatch alarm using the appropriate InputTokenCount statistic and period. CloudWatch evaluates runtime metrics and triggers configured notifications or actions. Cost Explorer analyzes billing, and Budgets tracks cost/usage against budgets; neither is this metric alarm.

options.name: Amazon CloudWatch metric alarm
options.when: Alert on runtime metrics and measured application signals.
options.trap: Choose the metric statistic and interval; not every quality metric is built in.
options.action: Configure a CloudWatch alarm on the chosen InputTokenCount statistic with the required five-minute evaluation period.

options.name: AWS Cost Explorer
options.when: Analyze supported billing/usage, attribution, and forecasts.
options.trap: A billing report is not this runtime token metric alarm.
options.wrong: A billing report does not evaluate the specified five-minute operational token metric.
options.action: Create a Cost Explorer usage report with application attribution and review it on the monthly financial schedule.

options.name: AWS Budgets
options.when: Notify or apply supported actions around defined cost/usage budgets.
options.trap: A budget is not automatically a real-time model token-admission cap.
options.wrong: A monthly cost-budget notification uses a different measure and interval from the stated runtime threshold.
options.action: Configure a monthly AWS Budgets notification for application cost and connect it to the operations response process.

options.name: Distributed tracing
options.action: Add token-count annotations to individual X-Ray traces and inspect selected requests when operators suspect a surge.
options.when: Use traces to inspect individual request stages.
options.trap: Request-path evidence and a metric-threshold alarm are different mechanisms.
options.wrong: A trace annotation alone does not configure the requested CloudWatch metric alarm.

flow: Bedrock runtime: emit InputTokenCount
CloudWatch metric: aggregate the required statistic and period
CloudWatch alarm: evaluate the defined threshold
Notification/action: signal operations when the alarm changes state
topics.change: Use Cost Explorer to analyze billed usage and attribution, or Budgets to track cost/usage against a defined spending plan.

name: Testing, Validation, and Troubleshooting
summary: Choose evidence, metrics, evaluators, and rollout methods for the specific defect.

topics.title: LLM judge vs. humans vs. automated metrics
topics.rule: Use semantic judging for scalable assessment, experts for calibrated labels/nuance, and assertions/metrics for targeted repeatable checks.
topics.question: A team must compare two Bedrock prompt versions on helpfulness and source support across 10,000 answers. Experts can label 200 representative examples but cannot review the complete dataset. The team has an explicit scoring rubric and deterministic checks for required fields. The answers use varied wording, so reference-text overlap is not the primary target. Some outputs are concise but omit an important condition. The team must compare scores by query cohort and inspect judge disagreements, rather than select the fastest prompt. Which evaluation plan best fits the semantic assessment at this scale?
topics.clue: Semantic judgments must scale beyond the available human-review capacity and remain calibrated to expert labels.
topics.why: Use an LLM-as-a-judge evaluation with the explicit rubric, calibrated against the expert-labeled sample. Run it over the larger dataset and inspect disagreements and cohort results alongside deterministic checks. This extends semantic assessment to the required scale without treating the judge’s scores as unquestionable truth.

options.name: Calibrated LLM-as-a-judge / Bedrock evaluation
options.when: Large-scale semantic quality assessment requires a rubric and calibration.
options.trap: A judge can be biased/wrong; scores are not unquestionable truth.
options.action: Calibrate a rubric-based LLM judge on the expert sample, score the larger dataset, and inspect cohorts alongside deterministic checks.

options.name: Expert review of every answer
options.when: High-risk/nuanced accountability or reference labeling dominates.
options.trap: Human review is slower and requires consistent guidelines.
options.wrong: Complete manual review exceeds the explicitly stated expert-review capacity.
options.action: Assign all 10,000 answers to expert reviewers and use their complete manual scoring as the required comparison.

options.name: BLEU/ROUGE overlap scores alone
options.when: Reference-text overlap is a suitable targeted regression signal.
options.trap: Word overlap does not establish source-supported helpfulness.
options.wrong: Text overlap does not directly establish helpfulness or whether claims are supported by the supplied sources.
options.action: Score every answer using BLEU/ROUGE against reference text and select the prompt with the highest overlap.

options.name: Operational latency metrics
options.action: Compare latency, token cost, and required-field success across the dataset and select the most efficient passing prompt.
options.when: Operational metrics measure performance and resource use.
options.trap: Efficiency does not establish semantic answer quality.
options.wrong: A faster or cheaper answer can still be unhelpful or unsupported, so these metrics do not assess the requested qualities.

flow: Evaluation set: answers, sources, and the scoring rubric
Expert sample: create reference judgments for calibration
Judge evaluation: score the full set and inspect disagreements
Release comparison: review semantic scores and deterministic-check results
topics.change: Prioritize expert review for high-risk cases and nuanced disagreements; use deterministic assertions for objectively checkable fields and tool outcomes.

topics.title: Precision vs. recall vs. faithfulness
topics.reference: Domain 5 RAG metric distinction · PDF pp. 33–39
topics.rule: Missing evidence, noisy retrieval, and unsupported generated claims are different failure boundaries.
topics.question: A Bedrock Knowledge Base returns all passages needed to answer a warranty question, with little irrelevant content. The generated answer nevertheless says every product qualifies, although the passages limit eligibility to specified plans. The citation links to a real retrieved passage, and the response parses successfully as JSON. The evaluation set includes warranty questions from multiple plans, and reviewers compare individual answer claims with the supplied policy conditions. The team wants to isolate answer quality rather than change an already-complete evidence set. Which evaluation measure most directly assesses this observed defect?
topics.clue: Required evidence is present, but the generated claim contradicts or exceeds that evidence.
topics.why: Evaluate answer faithfulness against the supplied passages. Faithfulness asks whether the answer’s claims are supported by its context, which directly targets the unsupported universal eligibility statement. Retrieval precision and recall assess the evidence set rather than whether the generator used it correctly.

options.name: Answer faithfulness / groundedness
options.when: Assess whether answer claims are supported by the supplied evidence.
options.trap: A real citation is not proof of entailment.
options.action: Evaluate faithfulness by checking material answer claims against the supplied warranty passages.

options.name: Retrieval/context precision
options.when: Measure relevance of the retrieved context or candidate set.
options.trap: Relevant chunks do not guarantee the model uses them faithfully.
options.wrong: The scenario already reports little irrelevant retrieval; relevant passages can still be used incorrectly during generation.
options.action: Evaluate retrieval precision by measuring the relevance of the retrieved warranty passages.

options.name: Retrieval/context recall
options.when: Assess coverage of required relevant evidence.
options.trap: Complete evidence can still produce an unsupported answer.
options.wrong: The needed passages are already present, so evidence coverage does not directly measure the unsupported generated claim.
options.action: Evaluate retrieval recall by measuring coverage of the warranty passages needed for the answer.

options.name: Schema validity
options.action: Evaluate schema and citation validity by checking required fields and whether cited source locations exist.
options.when: Structure checks enforce the output contract.
options.trap: A valid field can contain an unsupported claim.
options.wrong: Parsing proves structure, not that the warranty statement follows from the retrieved passage.

flow: Knowledge Bases retrieval: obtain the warranty conditions
Amazon Bedrock: produce the eligibility answer
Faithfulness evaluation: compare each material claim with those conditions
Review result: flag the unsupported universal eligibility statement
topics.change: Use recall when needed evidence is missing, or precision when irrelevant passages dominate the retrieved context.

topics.title: A/B vs. canary vs. shadow testing
topics.rule: Comparison, limited live exposure, and isolated mirrored traffic have different risk and feedback contracts.
topics.question: A team wants to compare a new Bedrock agent with the production version using copies of real requests. Users must continue to receive only the production answers. The candidate must not execute production writes, even when it proposes a tool action. The existing production agent performs legitimate writes, so simply hiding the candidate answer is insufficient. The comparison must preserve representative request context while isolating candidate effects. The team has not yet approved live candidate exposure. Which validation approach meets these constraints?
topics.clue: The candidate sees mirrored requests but must have neither live user delivery nor production side effects.
topics.why: Run an isolated shadow path using copied requests and sandboxed or suppressed write tools. Compare its outputs with the live path without returning candidate answers to users. A canary or live A/B cohort exposes users to candidate behavior, so neither matches the stated isolation requirement.

options.name: Isolated shadow evaluation
options.when: Compare mirrored production-like requests without using candidate results live.
options.trap: Mirrored writes must be sandboxed/suppressed; duplicating data/inference is not free.
options.action: Mirror requests to a shadow candidate with isolated/suppressed writes and compare its recorded output without user delivery.

options.name: Canary rollout
options.when: Limit production exposure to a small candidate cohort with rollback.
options.trap: Canary users actually receive candidate behavior.
options.wrong: Canary users receive candidate behavior, which violates the requirement that only production answers reach users.
options.action: Route a small canary cohort to the candidate, enforce normal tool permissions, and roll back if quality regresses.

options.name: Live A/B testing
options.when: Compare outcomes of assigned live variants after safety gates.
options.trap: No fixed 50/50 split is required, but users receive their variant.
options.wrong: A live candidate A/B group is exposed to candidate answers and potentially actions, contrary to the required isolation.
options.action: Assign live requests to controlled A/B variants, retain normal tool permissions, and compare the observed user outcomes.

options.name: Shadow with live write tools
options.action: Mirror requests to the candidate and hide its answers while preserving production write tools to test realistic behavior.
options.when: A shadow path must isolate both output delivery and harmful side effects.
options.trap: Hidden answers do not make duplicate production writes safe.
options.wrong: This suppresses user-visible output but still violates the explicit prohibition on candidate production writes.

flow.start: Production request: execute the live path and mirror a copy
flow.branchLabel: Only one path serves the user
branches: Production agent: return the live answer and enforce normal tool policy
Shadow candidate: collect its answer and suppress or sandbox writes
flow.end: Evaluation: compare outputs and tool proposals without candidate user delivery

topics.change: After offline and shadow gates pass, a canary can limit live exposure with rollback; A/B testing fits a controlled comparison of live variant outcomes.

topics.title: Stale index vs. chunking vs. generation
topics.rule: Inspect the first broken evidence boundary; do not infer a universal root cause from a similarity score.
topics.question: A company replaced an approved policy document in S3 yesterday. Bedrock Knowledge Bases Retrieve still returns a passage tagged with the old source version. The passage is coherent, and the model accurately repeats it. The replacement source contains a changed eligibility condition. The trace shows an old source-version identifier, rather than a low similarity score or a truncated current passage. The team wants to correct the first demonstrated inconsistency before tuning later stages. Which investigation should the team perform first?
topics.clue: The source is current, but retrieval demonstrably returns an older indexed version.
topics.why: Check the Knowledge Bases ingestion/synchronization status and whether the update or deletion reached the relevant index. The first observed mismatch is between source and indexed evidence. Chunk-size changes and generation tuning cannot make an unchanged old index reflect the new policy.

options.name: Knowledge Bases synchronization
options.when: Indexed source versions differ from approved current documents.
options.trap: An S3 object change alone does not prove completed ingestion.
options.action: Inspect ingestion synchronization, failed updates/deletes, and source-version metadata, then verify the replacement reaches retrieval.

options.name: Chunking configuration
options.when: Correctly extracted/indexed content loses needed meaning at chunk boundaries.
options.trap: Chunk size is not the automatic cause of old document versions.
options.wrong: The old passage is coherent; changing chunk boundaries does not address the demonstrated source-version mismatch without a proper index refresh.
options.action: Increase chunk size and regenerate chunks from the already indexed old content before retesting the same question.

options.name: Generation parameters
options.when: Output variability is the measured defect with adequate current context.
options.trap: Sampling cannot update stale private evidence.
options.wrong: The model is already repeating its context accurately, so sampling changes do not supply the updated policy.
options.action: Reduce model temperature and strengthen instructions to use the most recent policy available in the unchanged context.

options.name: Reranking
options.action: Rerank the current candidate passages and return the highest-ranked policy to the generator.
options.when: Rerank candidate evidence when ordering is the defect.
options.trap: Rank does not establish source freshness.
options.wrong: Rescoring outdated candidates does not ingest the replacement source version.

flow: Amazon S3: confirm the approved current policy version
Knowledge Bases ingestion: inspect synchronization and failures
Index handling: update/remove affected old chunks
Retrieve verification: confirm the current version is returned
topics.change: If the current source is indexed but its exception is split out of context, investigate chunking or context assembly; if current context is supplied but misused, investigate generation.

topics.title: Bedrock evaluation vs. Clarify vs. monitoring
topics.rule: FM answer evaluation, supported ML bias/explainability analysis, and operational monitoring have different roles.
topics.question: A team has two Bedrock RAG configurations and a held-out dataset of questions, retrieved context, and generated responses. It wants a managed comparison using supported relevance and faithfulness metrics with a judge model. Operational dashboards already show latency and token cost. Both candidate configurations use supported evaluation resources, and the team needs quality scores tied to this dataset before promotion. Feature-attribution analysis is not the release criterion. Which AWS capability is the most direct fit?
topics.clue: The task is managed assessment of FM/RAG response quality on a supplied evaluation dataset.
topics.why: Use a supported Bedrock RAG evaluation job with the required dataset and judge configuration. It scores the answer qualities specified in the question and produces results for the comparison. Clarify addresses supported ML bias/explainability workflows, while CloudWatch can monitor emitted results rather than create these semantic judgments.

options.name: Bedrock model/RAG evaluations
options.when: Run supported FM or RAG answer-quality evaluations.
options.trap: Available jobs/metrics/resources are service-specific; verify support.
options.action: Run supported Bedrock RAG evaluation jobs on the held-out dataset with the configured judge and quality metrics.

options.name: SageMaker Clarify
options.when: Supported ML pipelines need bias metrics or explainability analysis.
options.trap: Bias/feature explanations are not interchangeable with FM faithfulness scoring.
options.wrong: Feature attribution and supported bias/explainability analysis are different from the requested RAG relevance/faithfulness judge evaluation.
options.action: Run SageMaker Clarify feature-attribution analysis and use the explanations to rank the RAG configurations.

options.name: CloudWatch metrics alone
options.when: Track emitted quality/operations signals and alert on change.
options.trap: A dashboard does not itself create calibrated answer-quality scores.
options.wrong: A dashboard displays measurements; it does not itself generate the semantic judgments required for this dataset.
options.action: Build a CloudWatch dashboard from existing latency/token signals and use the dashboard to assign response-quality scores.

options.name: CloudTrail audit
options.action: Compare CloudTrail model-call audit records for both configurations and use successful calls as the quality assessment.
options.when: Use audit events to establish API activity and caller evidence.
options.trap: Caller activity is not semantic scoring of response content.
options.wrong: The audit trail does not perform the requested context-and-answer judge assessment.

flow: Held-out dataset: questions, context, and responses for both configurations
Bedrock RAG evaluation: apply the supported judge and metrics
Evaluation results: compare relevance and faithfulness by cohort
Release decision: assess results against the agreed quality gates
topics.change: Use Clarify for a supported ML bias/explainability assessment, or CloudWatch when the task is monitoring and alarming on already emitted operational or quality signals.

topics.title: GenAI Lens vs. general framework vs. MLOps
topics.reference: PDF trap 16 · cross-domain review; blueprint Domain 1, skill 1.1.3
topics.rule: Use GenAI-specific lifecycle guidance within the six-pillar Well-Architected framework.
topics.question: An architecture review must cover a GenAI application’s model selection, RAG, safety, deployment, token economics, and continuous improvement using AWS Well-Architected guidance. The team wants a lifecycle-wide review rather than only model deployment automation. The application combines a managed model, retrieved private data, tool integrations, and monitored production releases. The review must consider tradeoffs across the established six pillars and produce prioritized improvements, not merely confirm that an automation job succeeded. Which approach best meets this requirement?
topics.clue: The requested guidance spans the GenAI lifecycle within the Well-Architected framework.
topics.why: Apply the Generative AI Lens alongside the six-pillar Well-Architected Framework. The Lens adds GenAI-specific review guidance across the lifecycle. A deployment pipeline automates steps, but does not replace that architecture review; the Lens also does not replace the framework’s pillars.

options.name: Well-Architected + GenAI Lens
options.when: Review GenAI architecture/lifecycle with the six Well-Architected pillars.
options.trap: GenAI topics are not replacement pillars.
options.action: Use the Well-Architected Framework with the Generative AI Lens and turn lifecycle review findings into prioritized improvements.

options.name: SageMaker Pipelines
options.when: Automate supported ML processing, evaluation, and deployment steps.
options.trap: A pipeline is not the whole GenAI architecture-review framework.
options.wrong: Successful automation does not assess the full set of model, data, safety, cost, and operational architecture requirements.
options.action: Use SageMaker Pipelines to automate evaluation and deployment and treat passing executions as the complete architecture review.

options.name: Application components
options.when: Document the application’s concrete model, data, and runtime components.
options.trap: A component list is not a replacement for the Well-Architected pillars.
options.wrong: GenAI components are review subjects, not a replacement for the established six-pillar framework.
options.action: Create a review checklist of model, vector store, and runtime components and replace the established pillar-based review with it.

options.name: General review without the Lens
options.action: Use the general Well-Architected questions without the available GenAI Lens and focus the review on generic infrastructure checks.
options.when: General framework guidance remains the architecture foundation.
options.trap: A relevant Lens adds workload-specific questions to the general review.
options.wrong: The requirement explicitly asks for GenAI-specific lifecycle coverage, which the applicable Lens directly supplies.

flow: GenAI architecture: define model, data, and operational choices
Generative AI Lens: review lifecycle concerns across the framework
Review findings: identify quality, safety, and operational gaps
Improvement plan: prioritize and verify corrective work
topics.change: Use SageMaker Pipelines when the requirement is to automate supported ML lifecycle steps; retain architecture review as a separate assessment.
